label: 🌑 아디레 엘레코 — 40대 마당
prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, full body shot.
Model: one woman in her forties, full curvy figure, broad hips and defined waist, strong shoulders, hair in tight cornrows gathered back.
Pose: standing with weight on one leg, one hand resting on the outward hip, the other arm hanging, torso turned three-quarter, chin lifted.

Body fully painted with: Yoruba adire eleko — deep indigo ground with pale cassava-paste resist patterns. Olokun concentric ring motifs across the torso, ibadandun grid squares filled with tiny hand-drawn symbols over the hips and thighs, fine comb-drawn line bands down the arms. Every square of the grid filled with a different small motif, no blank ground. Soft irregular bleed at the edges where the resist lifted.

Pigment applied directly on bare skin, matte, pores and skin texture visible.
The paint ends at the wrist and ankle in a thin crisp border; hands and feet bare.
Hands fully visible, five separated fingers each.

Barefoot on packed earth.
Environment: a compound courtyard, indigo dye pots, cloth drying on a line.
Lighting: late afternoon sun from the side at a low angle, raking hard across the body to model the hip and waist, warm bounce off the earth on the shadow side.
Style: documentary photography of textile craft. ultra-sharp 8K. portrait 2:3 vertical.
